title: Park the advice the host never answers

blocks.text: This picks up where the previous practice ended. The file already contains its solution.

An advice that the host never answers would sit at the front of the line forever, and every advice behind it would wait too. The network allows a fixed number of attempts per advice. After the last one, the advice goes to a second table, `parked`, where an operator deals with it, and the line moves on.

Finish `notAnswered` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/AdviceSaf.java`. The `Store` rows already have an `attempts` column. The tests restart the SAF between attempts, and they also keep the link down for a while. About 7 lines.

cases.says: an advice the host never answers stops being retried, and the advice behind it is delivered
a parked advice is kept for an operator, never deleted
the attempt count is stored with the advice, so a restart does not grant fresh attempts
only attempts that went out count; time with the link down does not
with a limit of three, the third attempt is made before the advice is parked
with a limit of two, an advice is parked after its second unanswered attempt, with no third

origin.section: 12.7 A Reversal Must Outlive the Process and Wait Its Turn

concepts: A message the host never answers is parked after the allowed attempts, with the count stored alongside it, so it neither blocks the line nor gets deleted.
